full_judgment:
2. The petitioner Nos. 1, 3-5 and late Ali Azam, the predecessor-in-interest of petitioner Nos. 2(a) to 2(i) as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 706/81 on 23.12.81 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Noakhali for declaration of their title by adverse possession in the suit land measuring 27.73 acres against the opposite parties and others. The suit was decreed on compromise against defendant Nos. 1-3 and ex parte against other defendants including the opposite parties on 28.8.82. Thereafter on 14.7.83 the opposite parties filed an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte decree and upon the said application Miscellaneous Case No.141/83 was registered on 9.4.84 after receipt of the record from the Record Room. 

 3. Opposite-parties herein filed the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case for setting aside the ex parte decree against them on the allegations, inter alia that the summons of the suit were not served upon them and the plaintiffs suppressed the same by unduly influencing the process server and obtained a false return of service in collusion with their own men as attesting witnesses. Had the defendants an opportunity to contest the suit, the suit could not have been decreed and the plaintiffs in collusion with their party men defendant Nos. 1-3 filed a fraudulent petition of compromise; that it is apparent from the return of the service of summons that the same were not served and have been suppressed; that the defendant-petitioners opposite parties herein did not know about the said ex parte decree and when plaintiff No.1 threatened the present opposite party No. 2 on 16.6.83 saying that they should not enter into the suit property as he obtained a decree of perpetual injunction and after hearing the same defendant-petitioner No.2 made enquiry on 21.6.83 and came to know on 22.6.83 on receipt of information from the Court that the plaintiffs obtained an ex parte decree on 16.1.83 in Title Suit No. 167/82 and thereafter on further enquiry came to know on 10.7.83 that they obtained an ex parte decree on 28.8.82 in Title Suit No. 706/81 and thereafter they filed the Miscellaneous Case on 14.7.83. 

 8. It appears from the impugned order that the Court below considered Ext. Ka(2), the return dated 11.1.82 of the service of summons of defendant Nos. 1, 4-8 and came to the conclusion that the service was not satisfactory, It appears from the said return that defendant No. 1 received the summons by signing his name and defendant Nos. 4, 5 and 7 were not present at their residence and the process-server tendered the summons on defendant No.8 for him and for defendant Nos. 4, 5 and 7 and he having refused to accept the same the process server served their summons with copy of plaint by hanging on 11.1.82. But there is no verified declaration of the process server under Order 5 rule 17 of the Code. There is no explanation about non-service of summons on defendant No. 6. Thereafter the Nazir made an endorsement on 16.1.82 of due service of summons upon the said defendant Nos. 1, 5, 7 and 8. It appears from the Order No.2 dated 3.2.82 that summons of the suit was served on the defendants and Court fixed the same for ex parte hearing on 14.3.82 as none of the defendants entered appearance overlooking that no summons was served on defendant No.6 and summons on defendant Nos. 4, 5, 7 and 8 was served by hanging under rule 17 of Order 5 of the Code. It was, therefore incumbent on the Court below to make an enquiry under rule 19 of Order 5 of the Code and record a distinct declaration of due service, if satisfied, or to order service afresh. This view finds support from the case of Mst. Johara Begum vs. Rafiqul Kader reported in 25 DLR 91. But the Court below without doing so fixed the suit for ex parte hearing. Defendant No.8 deposing as PW 1 denied that the process-server even tendered summons to him or he refused to accept the same whereas the process server deposing as DW 1 supported the said return of the service of summons. It appears from the impugned order that the Court below after considering the oral evidence of the PWs as well as DW 1 allowed the Miscellaneous Case on the view that the service of summons was not satisfactory and the opposite parties should get a chance to contest the suit. We have already noticed that no summons was served upon the defendant No. 6 and as such the suit could not be taken up for ex parte disposal on 28.8.82. Moreover, the Court below as the Court of fact has jurisdictiontorely on the evidence of PWs and not to rely on the evidence of DW 1 regarding service of summons. It is true in doing so Court below did not discuss the evidence of the said witnesses and assign reason for the same. But the fact remains that the Court which passed the impugned order recorded evidence of the said witnesses and heard the said witnesses deposing and also noticed their demeanours. In that view of the matter we find no fault in the Court below for not discussing the evidence of the witnesses in passing the impugned order. Court below, having found service of summons not satisfactory, gave the defendant-opposite parties herein a chance to contest the suit and, as such, we find no illegality resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in setting aside the said ex parte decree.
